t:
(a) Strategic Plan Required.—Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act and not less often than once every 2 fiscal years thereafter until September 30, 2022, the Director of the Defense Information Systems Agency, in consultation with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics and the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense, shall develop or update, as appropriate, a strategic plan for the Agency that includes—
        (1) a comprehensive review of the requirements and mission of the Agency with respect to research, development, test, and evaluation; and 
        (2) an assessment of the adequacy of the activities, facilities, workforce, and resources of the Agency in meeting such requirements and fulfilling such mission.  
    (b) Covered Period.—Each strategic plan under subsection (a) shall cover the period of five fiscal years beginning with the fiscal year in which the plan is developed or updated. 
    (c) Elements.—Each strategic plan under subsection (a) shall include the following elements:
        (1) A statement of the mission of the Defense Information Systems Agency that—
            (A) addresses the critical operations and functions carried out by the Agency; and 
            (B) includes an assessment of projected changes to such operations and functions for the period covered by the plan.  
        (2) An assessment of the personnel, facilities, and research, development, test, and evaluation requirements of the Department of Defense that are needed to support the operations of the Agency for the period covered by the plan. 
        (3) An identification of performance metrics for measuring the successful achievement of objectives for the period covered by the plan. 
        (4) An assessment of the programs and plans of the Agency with respect to research, development, test, and evaluation, including the projected resources, personnel, and supporting infrastructure needed to carry out such programs and plans. 
        (5) An assessment of the facilities and resources of the Agency that are used for research, development, test, and evaluation activities. 
        (6) A description of the plans and business case analyses supporting any significant modifications to the facilities, workforce, and resources of the Agency (including any modifications involving the expansion, divestment, consolidation, or curtailment of activities) that are proposed, projected, or recommended by the Director. 
        (7) Any other matters determined to be appropriate by the Director.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the phrase "in consultation with" signals participation. But the only parties consulted are the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics and the DoD Chief Information Officer, who are federal officials, so this is intra-government coordination. Nothing in the section involves states, experts, the public, or any other outside party, and it does not require rulemaking, hearings, or grant a right to sue.
fable.s: the Director of the Defense Information Systems Agency, in consultation with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics and the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense, shall develop or update, as appropriate, a strategic plan for the Agency

opus.w: The only consultation required is among Department of Defense officials, so it is coordination within the federal government, not participation by outsiders. The keyword "consultation" is tempting, but no state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public takes part in developing the strategic plan. The rest of the section only lists what the plan must contain.
opus.s: the Director of the Defense Information Systems Agency, in consultation with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics and the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense, shall develop or update, as appropriate, a strategic plan for the Agency
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The phrase "in consultation with" makes this look like participation. But every party named is inside the federal government: the Director of DISA, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics, and the DoD Chief Information Officer. Nothing else in the section brings in an outside party. There is no public comment, no hearing, no advisory board and no consultation with states.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Director to consult with other federal officials (Under Secretary of Defense and CIO) to develop a strategic plan. Since all parties involved are inside the federal government, this is intra-agency coordination, not participation by outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: the Director of the Defense Information Systems Agency, in consultation with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics and the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense, shall develop or update, as appropriate, a strategic plan
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "consultation" implies participation. However, the parties consulted (Under Secretary of Defense, Chief Information Officer) are all high-ranking federal officials inside the Department of Defense. Intra-governmental coordination does not constitute participation under the definition.
